what: Measured metabolic rates of people walking or running on a treadmill in a pressurised planetary spacesuit (NASA Mark III) and matched unsuited controls, in simulated lunar (1/6 g), Mars (3/8 g) and other reduced gravity levels, from NASA Johnson Space Center EVA Physiology reports. Values marked 'estimated from figure' were read by us from the report's plotted trend lines and carry the stated reading error. Conversions to watts use an assumed 20.1 J per ml O2. Collected 2026-11-14 for model validation.

points.page: PDF p.14 (slide 14); same mean in EWT2007 PDF p.17 text
points.where: Slide 14 table '10 km Walkback Summary Data (averaged across entire 10 km unless noted)'; EWT2007 'Summary of Preliminary Results'
points.suit: Mark III (MKIII) Advanced Space Suit Technology Demonstrator with PLSS mock-up and spider-gimbal
points.pressure: 4.3 psig (EWT2007 PDF p.7: 'All suited tests were performed at 4.3 psig')
points.gravity_method: POGO partial gravity simulator (pneumatic overhead offload via gimbal); combined weight of subject, LCG, suit, PLSS mock-up and gimbal offloaded to 1/6 g (EWT2007 PDF p.6)
points.weight_definition: Offload applied to subject + LCG + suit + PLSS mock-up + gimbal so their combined weight equals lunar weight. Suit mass: EWT2008 slide 5 says '121 kg total suit weight'. EWT2007 gives MKIII about 54 kg (120 lb) (p.7), PLSS mock-up 40 lb and gimbal 95 lb (p.6), but also gimbal 'approximately 40.8 kgs (90 lbs)' (p.8): the parts do not add to 121 kg. Body mass 81.4 +/- 7.8 kg (EWT2008 slide 4); 179.5 +/- 17.3 lb (EWT2007 Table 1, p.9).
points.speed_reported: 3.94 mph average (EWT2007 p.17); 3.9 +/- 0.5 mph (EWT2008 slide 14). Self-selected and varied over time (Figure 5 / slide 14 plot).

measured.unit: BTU/h

points.conversion: 1 BTU/h = 0.29307107 W (International Table BTU). Whole-body gross rate as measured by the suit CO2 method; not normalised to mass.
points.read_from: table (slide 14) and text (EWT2007 p.17)
points.notes: Duration 95.8 min (SD 13). Max 15-min average 2617 BTU/h (SD 315) = 767.0 W. Total energy 944.2 kcal (SD 70.5). Avg 50.8% VO2pk (SD 6.1%). Slide 14 also lists 'Energy expenditure 599 kcal/hr' and O2 usage 0.4 lb/h. Level treadmill (no incline capability, EWT2007 p.9). EWT2007 says the rate is ~10 kcal/min. Suited metabolic rate was estimated from suit ventilation and exhaust CO2 using each subject's VCO2-VO2 regression (EWT2007 p.15), not measured O2 uptake. Gait not reported for the walkback; subjects chose their own pace.

facts.statement: Suited locomotion had higher metabolic rates than unsuited and unsuited weight-matched controls; locomotion at Mars gravity required higher rates than at Moon gravity, suited and unsuited.
The MKIII suit 'functioned acceptably throughout all speeds on the Moon, but was extremely limited on Mars'.
Lunar suited transport cost (ml O2/kg/km) decreased as speed increased and levelled off around 4 mph.
facts.page: PDF p.15; also EWT2007 PDF p.17

facts.statement: Both the average (2374 BTU/h) and the maximum 15-min average (2617 BTU/h) walkback metabolic rates exceed Apollo and EMU cooling capabilities; all subjects said they would have walked faster but were limited by cooling.

Walk-to-run: each subject's preferred transition speed (PTS) was found at 1/6 g and 3/8 g (EWT) and data were taken at 3 walking and 3 running speeds placed around it, avoiding the transition zone. The reports read do not give the PTS values in numbers. The EWT paper states that walking at a true running speed costs more than running at that speed (and vice versa), which was used to confirm the PTS.
Suited running speed increments were set at half those of the unsuited trials (0.5 vs 1.0 mph) 'due to the difficulty of moving the MKIII suit at higher speeds'.

Suited metabolic rate was not measured by gas exchange: it was estimated from suit ventilation rate, exhaust CO2 and the regression between VCO2 and VO2 from each subject's VO2peak test. Unsuited rate used a metabolic cart (EWT, IST-1) or COSMED K4b2 (IST-2).
facts.page: PDF p.25 (printed p.10); also EWT2007 p.15, IST1_2008 p.4

facts.statement: Metabolic rates are the highest 1-minute average during each 3-minute stage, expressed per kg of the subject's body mass (ml O2/kg/min).
facts.page: PDF p.4; same in IST2_TP2010 PDF p.25 (printed p.10)

facts.statement: IST-1 (level, 1/6 g): varying suit pressure from 6.9 to 44.8 kPa did not significantly change metabolic rate; the largest difference (6.9 vs 34.5 kPa) ranged from 0 to 3.0 ml/kg/min across speeds.

IST-1 (level, varied weight at fixed 121 kg suit mass): below 4.0 km/h the lightest-to-heaviest suit weight difference was 2.85 ml/kg/min (not significant, threshold 3.5); above 4 km/h it rose from about 6 ml/kg/min (4.0-5.0 km/h) to about 15 ml/kg/min (6.1-8.0 km/h). Weights tested correspond to 0.12, 0.167, 0.22, 0.27 and 0.32 g.
IST-1: suit cost unrelated to weight (suited minus weight-matched unsuited) was not significant for 1-g-equivalent suit weights of 63 to 186 kg but rose significantly above 186 kg.
IST-1 metabolic rates were consistently lower than in the Walkback Test for the 3 repeat subjects (proposed reasons: familiarisation, larger treadmill, better weigh-out).

IST-2 (inclined, suited, varied gravity 0.12-0.32 g): mean difference between highest and lowest weight conditions was 1.9 ml/kg/min at 0% (IST-1 level data), 3.5 at 10%, 8.7 at 20% and 17.0 at 30% grade.

IST-2: the metabolic cost of weight increased with grade, but the cost unrelated to weight decreased with grade; suited and weight-matched unsuited lines converged at 30% grade. The authors attribute this mainly to artificial assistance from the POGO (subjects kept the trunk upright on inclines, which would not normally be possible).
IST-2 Earth Shirtsleeve Performance Index (suited 1/6 g rate divided by 1-g unsuited rate) for incline walking: 1.0 +/- 0.2 at 10%, 0.8 +/- 0.2 at 20%, 0.6 +/- 0.1 at 30% grade.
IST-2 load carry (level, lowest walking speed, 1/6 g): suited minus unsuited metabolic rate averaged 7.2, 7.1 and 10.0 ml/kg/min for 10, 20 and 30 lb loads (n = 5).

IST-2 regression for suited incline walking: MR = b0 + b1(V x G) + b2 Lshank + b3 Lshoulder + b4 Psuit + b5 Msuit, MR in L O2/min, V in m/s, G in %, lengths in cm, Psuit in kPa, Msuit in kg; pseudo R2 = 0.668; residuals mostly +/- 0.30 L/min. The coefficient values b0-b5 are NOT printed in the report (UNVERIFIED). Valid only for 0.56-0.97 m/s, 0-30% grade and the Table 7 conditions.
IST-2: practical significance threshold 3.5 ml/kg/min, equal to 0.30 L/min for an 82 kg subject; no inferential statistics because n = 6.

IST-2: the report states that a primary limitation is the inability to compare shirtsleeve with suited results to quantify the effect of the suit, because suspension methods and metabolic measurement systems differed.
IST-2: weight was varied by changing offload; mass was not. All suited varied-weight trials used the 121 kg suit; the report says results cannot be assumed to reflect varied suit mass.
IST-2 inclined walking: baseline shirtsleeve cost was about 50% of suited metabolic cost independent of grade; suit pressure was a minor component.

IST series review: increased suit weight gave significantly higher VO2 at speeds >= 5.0 km/h on a level treadmill and at grades >= 20% at slow walking speeds of 2.7 +/- 0.6 km/h; varying suit pressure caused no significant change for any task; varying inertial mass (unsuited) showed no significant change.
IST series review: in 1-g conditions, walking over unknown lunar-like terrain (HMP) raised metabolic rate by 56% on average (range 41-67%) and distance by 7% (up to 21%).
During reduced-gravity POGO trials the subject's limbs still operated in a 1-g field (only the torso is offloaded).
